name: Iddo
overview: Iddo was a male seer known for having visions concerning Jeroboam, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 9:29. Beyond his role as a prophet, Scripture does not provide additional details about his tribal affiliation or other personal notes. His prophetic insight marks him as a significant figure in the biblical narrative.
namesAndTitles: The name Iddo likely means 'YHWH has adorned,' reflecting a divine association in its Hebrew origin. This proper name does not appear to have been given directly by God but still carries a meaningful theophoric element.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Iddo beyond what is noted in his unique attribute as a seer. There are no listed connections to other individuals in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Iddo's importance in Scripture stems from his prophetic visions concerning Jeroboam, which contribute to the historical and spiritual understanding of this period in Israel's history. His role as a seer highlights God's ongoing communication with His people through chosen prophets. Though details are sparse, his mention underscores the faithfulness of God’s revelation during the reign of Jeroboam.
